newsitem.title: GERMANY: Dresden Jews plan to build new synagogue.
newsitem.headline: Dresden Jews plan to build new synagogue.

text.p: Jews in the eastern German city of Dresden said on Monday they would build a new synagogue near the site of the original, razed to the ground by the Nazis on "Kristallnacht" in 1938.
The Nazis looted more than 7,000 Jewish shops and burned hundreds of synagogues across Germany on November 9, 1938, a date otherwise known as "the night of broken glass."

Protestant and Catholic churches as well as political, economic and cultural leaders gave backing to the plan to rebuild the synagogue. It will cost about 20 million marks ($13 million), financed by donations from home and abroad.

Dresden's Mayor Herbert Wagner and Saxony premier Kurt Biedenkopf announced their support for the project at a meeting to launch the fund-raising drive. "This is an attempt to heal the wounds of the past," Wagner said.
About 130 Jews now live in Dresden, compared with 6,000 at the start of the 1930s.
